title: backlog.py dispatch --resume ID sends a stopped or returned worker back with a message and moves its run state, so no orchestrator resumes a session by hand
goal: backlog.py dispatch --resume ID --message FILE resumes the worker session of the item's last dispatch (claude -p --resume, detached, the worker env and caps) and moves the run key to working and then to returned or failed as dispatch does

run: import subprocess,sys;r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/backlog.py','dispatch','-h'],capture_output=True,text=True);sys.exit(0 if r.returncode==0 and '--resume' in r.stdout else 1)

notes: Retrospective of SP-hja7yu5k: ST-fb7nlvke's landing stopped at checks, the orchestrator resumed the worker with a hand-built claude -p --resume (env KB_ROLE and KB_OPERATOR, caps, detached Popen) and moved the run key with coord.py transition (refused to working, then returned) because only dispatch moves it. The check only reads the help text for the flag: a planned item adds a planted run with a stub claude.
